questions.title: Match Digit at Start
questions.description:
Determine if a string begins with a digit.

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
`YES` if the string starts with a digit, else `NO`.

Constraints:
String length 1..100, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s =~ /^\d/ ? "YES" : "NO"

questions.title: Count Vowels via Scan
questions.description:
Count the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) in a string using `scan`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
The integer count of vowels.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.scan(/[aeiou]/i).size

questions.title: Replace Digits with X
questions.description:
Replace every digit in a string with the character `X` using `gsub`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
The string with all digits replaced by `X`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.gsub(/\d/, "X")

questions.title: Extract First Number
questions.description:
Extract the first sequence of digits from a string using `match`. If no digits exist, print `NONE`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
The first digit sequence, or `NONE`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
m = s.match(/\d+/)
puts m ? m[0] : "NONE"

questions.title: Has Letter Anchor
questions.description:
Determine if a string contains at least one letter (a-z, case-insensitive).

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
`YES` if at least one letter exists, else `NO`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts /[a-z]/i =~ s ? "YES" : "NO"

questions.title: Replace Whitespace With Underscore
questions.description:
Replace every whitespace character (space or tab) in a string with `_` using `gsub`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
The string with each whitespace char replaced by `_`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.gsub(/\s/, "_")

questions.title: Email Masker
questions.description:
A privacy tool masks the local part of an email address: keep the first and last character, replace the middle with `***`. Read an email, capture the local and domain parts, print the masked email. If the input is not a valid email (no single `@`), print `INVALID`.

Input Format:
Line 1: an email address.

Output Format:
`<first>***<last>@<domain>` or `INVALID`.

Constraints:
Input length 1..100, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
email = gets.chomp
if email =~ /^([^@]+)@([^@]+)$/
  local = $1
  domain = $2
  masked = local[0] + "***" + local[-1] + "@" + domain
  puts masked
else
  puts "INVALID"
end

questions.title: Phone Number Validator
questions.description:
Validate a US-style phone number against the pattern `NNN-NNN-NNNN` (three digits, dash, three digits, dash, four digits).

Input Format:
Line 1: a phone number string.

Output Format:
`VALID` if it matches exactly, else `INVALID`.

Constraints:
Input length 1..50, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s =~ /^\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}$/ ? "VALID" : "INVALID"

questions.title: Hashtag Extractor
questions.description:
A social-media tool extracts hashtags (a `#` followed by word characters) from a tweet. Print each hashtag on its own line in order of appearance. If none, print `(none)`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a tweet string.

Output Format:
One hashtag per line, or `(none)`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
tags = s.scan(/#\w+/)
if tags.empty?
  puts "(none)"
else
  tags.each { |t| puts t }
end

questions.title: Snake to Camel Converter
questions.description:
A code formatter converts `snake_case` identifiers to `camelCase`. Replace each `_<letter>` with the uppercase form of the letter.

Input Format:
Line 1: a snake_case identifier (lowercase letters and underscores).

Output Format:
The camelCase version.

Constraints:
Length 1..50, lowercase letters and underscores only.
questions.inputconstrains: Length 1..50, lowercase letters and underscores only

questions.title: Extract All Numbers Sum
questions.description:
A log parser extracts all integers (including negative) from a free-text line and prints their sum using `scan`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a string that may contain integers.

Output Format:
The integer sum of all integers found.

Constraints:
String length 1..200; integers in range -100000..100000; at least one integer present.
questions.inputconstrains: String length 1..200; integers in range -100000..100000; at least one integer present
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
nums = s.scan(/-?\d+/).map(&:to_i)
puts nums.sum

questions.title: First Match Capture Report
questions.description:
A configuration line has the format `name=NAME age=AGE`. Use `match` to capture NAME and AGE, and print `Name: NAME, Age: AGE`. If the input does not match, print `No match`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a configuration string.

Output Format:
`Name: NAME, Age: AGE` or `No match`.

Constraints:
String length 1..100; NAME is letters only; AGE is digits only.
questions.inputconstrains: String length 1..100; NAME is letters only; AGE is digits only
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
m = s.match(/name=(\w+) age=(\d+)/)
if m
  puts "Name: #{m[1]}, Age: #{m[2]}"
else
  puts "No match"
end

questions.title: Redact Email Pattern
questions.description:
A redaction tool replaces email-like substrings with `[REDACTED]`. Use `gsub` to replace any pattern of `word.word@word.word` form (where word is `[\w.]+`).

Input Format:
Line 1: a string.

Output Format:
The string with emails replaced by `[REDACTED]`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode: puts gets.chomp.gsub(/[\w.]+@[\w.]+/, "[REDACTED]")

questions.title: Domain Extractor From URL
questions.description:
A web crawler extracts the domain from a URL. Read a URL of the form `http(s)://domain/path...` and print only the domain (the host). If the URL is invalid (does not start with `http://` or `https://`), print `INVALID`. Use `=~` with capture groups.

Input Format:
Line 1: a URL string.

Output Format:
The domain, or `INVALID`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
url = gets.chomp
if url =~ %r{https?://([^/]+)}
  puts $1
else
  puts "INVALID"
end

questions.title: Count Words Starting With Letter A
questions.description:
A text analyzer counts how many whole words start with the letter `a` (case-insensitive) using a word-boundary anchor. Words consist of word characters only.

Input Format:
Line 1: a sentence string.

Output Format:
The integer count of words starting with `a`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sampleinput1: An apple a day keeps a doctor away
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
words = s.scan(/\ba\w*/i)
puts words.size

questions.title: Capitalize First Letter Regex
questions.description:
A formatter capitalizes only the first letter of a sentence (if it is lowercase a-z). Use `sub` with a regex anchored at the start. Non-lowercase first characters should be left unchanged.

Input Format:
Line 1: a sentence string.

Output Format:
The sentence with the first lowercase letter (if any) uppercased.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
puts s.sub(/^[a-z]/) { |c| c.upcase }

questions.title: Log Pattern Extractor Multi-Capture
questions.description:
A log line has the format `[timestamp] LEVEL message`. Read n log lines. For each, capture LEVEL and message using `=~` with two capture groups. Print `LEVEL: message`. Lines that do not match the pattern print `INVALID`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Lines 2..n+1: log lines.

Output Format:
n lines, each `LEVEL: message` or `INVALID`.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; LEVEL is uppercase letters only; message length 1..100.
questions.sampleinput1:
2
[2024-01-01] INFO Server started
[2024-01-01] ERROR Disk full
questions.sampleoutput1:
INFO: Server started
ERROR: Disk full
questions.input1:
3
[t1] A alpha
[t2] B beta
[t3] C gamma
questions.output1:
A: alpha
B: beta
C: gamma
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50; LEVEL is uppercase letters only; message length 1..100
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  if line =~ /^\[[^\]]+\] (\w+) (.+)$/
    puts "#{$1}: #{$2}"
  else
    puts "INVALID"
  end
end

questions.title: Replace Repeated Words
questions.description:
A text cleaner collapses consecutive duplicate words (e.g., `the the cat sat sat`) into a single occurrence (e.g., `the cat sat`). Use `gsub` with a backreference. Match whole-word duplicates separated by whitespace.

Input Format:
Line 1: a sentence string.

Output Format:
The sentence with consecutive duplicate words collapsed.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sampleinput1: the the cat sat sat on mat
questions.input3: a a b b c c
questions.sourcecode: puts gets.chomp.gsub(/\b(\w+)\s+\1\b/, '\1')

questions.title: Hex Color Codes Extractor
questions.description:
A CSS preprocessor extracts hex color codes of the form `#RGB` (3 hex digits) or `#RRGGBB` (6 hex digits) from a style string. Use `scan`. Print each match on its own line; if none, print `(none)`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a CSS-like string.

Output Format:
One color per line, or `(none)`.

Constraints:
String length 1..200, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
s = gets.chomp
hexes = s.scan(/#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}\b/)
if hexes.empty?
  puts "(none)"
else
  hexes.each { |h| puts h }
end

questions.title: Password Strength Validator
questions.description:
A password policy requires: length at least 8; at least one letter; at least one digit; at least one special character from `@#$%`. Use `=~` checks (no scan/match/gsub/sub) to validate. Print `STRONG` if all four conditions are met, else `WEAK`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a password string.

Output Format:
`STRONG` or `WEAK`.

Constraints:
Password length 1..50, printable ASCII.
questions.sourcecode:
pw = gets.chomp
has_letter = pw =~ /[A-Za-z]/
has_digit = pw =~ /\d/
has_special = pw =~ /[@#$%]/
has_length = pw =~ /^.{8,}$/
if has_letter && has_digit && has_special && has_length
  puts "STRONG"
else
  puts "WEAK"
end
